<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Enable adaptive DSpark verification for DeepSeek-V4.1 with PCP, building on #47808 and #61555. PCP needs exact query lengths on the CPU, so this path agrees on each request's verification length before partitioning the batch.

## Claims

- Keep verification lengths consistent across TP/PCP ranks and CPU/GPU layouts.
- Improve C64 output throughput by **9.5%** in the matched H20 test below. Low-concurrency regressions are included.

## Validation

4× H20, TP1×PCP4/EP4, DSpark up to 5 tokens, Humming A8, shared Engram, 32K chunk, max 64 sequences, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`. Same source, runtime and launch configuration; only `enable_adaptive_verification` changes.

`vllm bench serve`: fixed real GSM8K prompts, 600–710 input tokens, forced 512-token output, temperature 1, warmed prefix cache (~94% hit). Three repeats; output throughput is mean (min–max), TPOT is the mean. C1 uses 32 requests per repeat; other points use 256.

| Concurrency | Fixed output tok/s | Adaptive output tok/s | Change | TPOT ms, fixed → adaptive |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 150.4 (148.8–151.5) | 146.6 (142.3–149.5) | -2.6% | 6.57 → 6.75 |
| 16 | 1,286.0 (1,268.9–1,295.1) | 1,256.7 (1,241.0–1,265.8) | -2.3% | 12.00 → 12.30 |
| 32 | 1,825.1 (1,795.8–1,844.9) | 1,862.5 (1,856.7–1,865.7) | +2.0% | 16.64 → 16.23 |
| 64 | 2,334.6 (2,315.7–2,356.4) | 2,556.4 (2,544.2–2,573.3) | +9.5% | 25.58 → 23.14 |

This is a short-input math workload, not the original internal SPEED-Bench subset or a long-context throughput claim.

- **Full GSM8K:** 1,319 questions, five-shot, temperature 0, C64, normal stopping. Fixed: **1,223/1,319 (92.72%)**; adaptive: **1,230/1,319 (93.25%)**. All evaluation prompt hashes match between arms. This does not establish an accuracy improvement.
- All benchmark requests completed, with no preemptions; runtime logs confirm FULL graph execution. Initial instrumented requests also passed `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` and exercised trimmed budgets with matching allocations on all four ranks.
- `pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_pcp_manager.py -q`: **136 passed**. Four-GPU TP1/PCP4 and TP2/PCP2 layout/consensus checks and pre-commit passed.
- One adaptive GSM8K case is added to the existing PCP CI job. Upstream B200 validation is pending.

<details>
<summary>Benchmark reproduction</summary>

Build `prompts.jsonl` from the first 256 GSM8K test questions, prefixing each with the first five training question/answer pairs. Format each pair as `Question: {question}\nAnswer: {answer}\n\n`, then append `Question: {test_question}\nAnswer:`. Store each resulting string under `prompt`.

Warm up with 64 requests at C32 and 256 output tokens, then prime all 256 prompts with one output token. Use the same cache salt in both fresh servers. Run this at C1/16/32/64, using seeds 1234/1235/1236:

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --model dsv41-pcp \
  --tokenizer /model --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --dataset-name custom --dataset-path prompts.jsonl \
  --custom-output-len 512 --num-prompts 256 --max-concurrency 64 \
  --temperature 1 --ignore-eos --disable-shuffle --skip-chat-template \
  --extra-body '{"seed":1234,"cache_salt":"pcp-adaptive-decode-v1"}' \
  --save-result --save-detailed
```

Use 32 prompts at C1. Both arms use the same target capture sizes: `1,2,4,5,6,8,10,12,16,20,24,32,40,48,64,80,96,128,160,192,256,320,384`.

</details>

## Details

Reuse the host confidences already copied by adaptive DSpark for the budget and per-request draft counts, then broadcast those counts across TP and PCP. Price the target using the largest PCP-local batch; the drafter remains replicated. Mixed prefill batches retain full verification, and the non-PCP allocation path is unchanged. The tradeoffs are stale per-request confidence and CPU collective overhead.

Unlike #62769, which excludes PCP, this supplies the exact host layout required by PCP. Depends on #61555; its changes remain visible until it merges. [Adaptive implementation only](https://github.com/xijiaat/vllm/commit/404fade8). Local H20 validation used complete main-based Python source plus #61554 for Engram sharing on the existing Artifactory binary runtime.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes, implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

@@ -57,6 +57,24 @@ Set `enable_adaptive_verification: false` to verify the full block for every req
 - Not supported with LoRA (the per-token LoRA mapping is built from CPU-side boundaries) or pipeline parallelism (cost curves and confidences exist only on the last rank).
 - Without a confidence head, `use_local_argmax_reduction` is rejected. The estimator needs the full draft logits, which local argmax reduction never materializes.
 
+## DeepSeek-V4.1 with PCP
+
+On NVIDIA GPUs, DeepSeek-V4.1 can use adaptive DSpark with prefill context
+parallelism and `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` or `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` CUDA graphs.
+The existing PCP restrictions still apply, including `PP=DP=DCP=1`.
+
+PCP uses the already-copied host confidences for both the total verification
+budget and each request's admitted draft count. All TP and PCP ranks agree on
+these counts before partitioning. This keeps the CPU and GPU query boundaries
+identical without adding a device-to-host wait. The target cost is indexed by
+the largest rank-local batch; the drafter remains replicated. Mixed prefill
+batches retain fixed-length verification.
+
+Enable `enable_adaptive_verification` in the existing DSpark speculative config;
+`num_speculative_tokens` remains the maximum draft length. Measure fixed and
+adaptive verification on the same workload: shorter verification is not
+necessarily faster at low concurrency.
+
 ## Tuning the cost profile
 
 Step costs are profiled against a synthetic KV context, 8192 tokens by default. Deployments serving much longer contexts may want to raise it so the profiled step reads a more realistic amount of cache (this matters a bit less for sparse attention models like DeepSeek-v4 since the cheap indexer is the main cost that scales with context length).

@@ -16,6 +16,70 @@ Depending on the use case, there are two possible strategies:
 
 Both approaches are under active development.
 
+### DeepSeek-V4.1 CUDA graphs
+
+DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash supports PCP CUDA graphs on NVIDIA CUDA using Model Runner V2
+and `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41`. Select the graph mode explicitly:
+
+- `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` uses full graphs for decode and breakable piecewise graphs
+  for prefill and mixed batches within the captured token sizes.
+- `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` uses full graphs for decode; prefill and mixed batches run
+  eagerly.
+- `NONE` disables CUDA graphs. Pure `FULL` and `PIECEWISE` modes are not
+  supported by this V4.1 PCP path.
+
+V4.1 uses breakable CUDA graphs rather than `torch.compile` graph splitting.
+Set `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1` for piecewise modes. Compilation `mode=0`
+(`NONE`) disables `torch.compile`, not CUDA graphs: `cudagraph_mode` controls
+graph execution separately.
+
+For example, a four-GPU TP1/PCP4 instance with fixed-length DSpark can use:
+
+```bash
+VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 \
+vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 \
+    --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 1 --prefill-context-parallel-size 4 \
+    --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend allgather_reducescatter \
+    --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41 \
+    --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5}' \
+    --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 32 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
+    --enable-prefix-caching --swa-bounded-replay --no-async-scheduling \
+    --compilation-config '{"mode":0,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[5,6,10,12,20,24,40,48,80,96,160,192,256,512,768,1024],"max_cudagraph_capture_size":1024}' \
+    --cudagraph-metrics
+```
+
+Capture sizes are token counts. The example covers a 4096-token prefill split
+across PCP4 with 1024 tokens per rank, plus padded DSpark draft and verification
+buckets. Mixed and uneven batches can have larger local token counts; batches
+outside the captured sizes run eagerly. The draft processes the restored
+global batch, so do not divide its capture budget by the PCP size. Increase the
+capture sizes when increasing the batch-token limit. Use `--cudagraph-metrics`
+to check actual `FULL` and `PIECEWISE` execution counts; the configured mode
+alone does not prove either path ran.
+
+The example enables automatic prefix caching, which PCP bounded replay requires,
+and SWA bounded replay. Large
+piecewise graphs use an eager break to select the bounded decoder replay batch,
+then run its matching inner graph when available; larger replay batches fall
+back to eager execution. Keep `cudagraph_decoder_replay` enabled (the default)
+to retain bounded trimming in piecewise graphs. Full graphs and piecewise
+graphs below `decoder_replay_trim_threshold` keep the whole batch. Prefix-cache
+hits and bounded trimming depend on the requests and are not guaranteed by
+enabling the flags alone.
+
+Omit `--speculative-config` for ordinary decoding. PCP continues to require
+PP=DP=DCP=1, text-only input, synchronous scheduling, and no KV connector or
+MegaMoE. Adaptive speculative verification is unsupported. Engram tables remain
+TP-sharded and replicated across PCP ranks; account for their host memory when
+choosing the TP/PCP split.
+
+Speculative full-graph replay requires flattened or variable-length indexer queries,
+including when a PCP rank owns no decode requests. On SM90, fixed DSpark with
+5 speculative tokens uses the flattened path; native multi-query shapes such
+as 1 or 3 speculative tokens are rejected for graph execution. Use eager mode
+for those shapes.
+
 ## Decode Context Parallel
 
 Due to the auto-regressive nature of decoding, every decoding step needs to compute a small amount of query tokens w.r.t. a large number of key/value tokens stored in the paged KV cache. The core of decode context parallel is how to shard the KV cache across GPUs.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Host-known adaptive query lengths for PCP partitioning."""
+
+import numpy as np
+
+from vllm.distributed.parallel_state import get_pcp_group, get_tp_group
+
+
+def select_pcp_drafts(
+    survival: np.ndarray,
+    scheduled_drafts: np.ndarray,
+    non_draft_tokens: np.ndarray,
+    cost_tables: tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray],
+    max_draft_budget: int,
+    pcp_size: int,
+    shard_decode_requests: bool,
+    has_prefill: bool,
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    """Price each candidate budget by its largest rank-local target batch."""
+    num_reqs, num_steps = survival.shape
+    valid = np.arange(num_steps)[None, :] < scheduled_drafts[:, None]
+    order = np.argsort(-survival[valid], kind="stable")[:max_draft_budget]
+    requests = np.broadcast_to(np.arange(num_reqs)[:, None], valid.shape)[valid][order]
+    if has_prefill:
+        # Keep the existing full-width verification policy for mixed batches.
+        budget = len(order)
+    else:
+        owners = np.arange(num_reqs) % pcp_size
+        if not shard_decode_requests:
+            owners.fill(0)
+        base_tokens = np.bincount(
+            owners, weights=non_draft_tokens, minlength=pcp_size
+        ).astype(np.int64)
+        rank_drafts = np.zeros((len(order) + 1, pcp_size), dtype=np.int64)
+        rank_drafts[1:] = np.cumsum(
+            owners[requests, None] == np.arange(pcp_size), axis=0
+        )
+        local_tokens = (base_tokens + rank_drafts).max(axis=1)
+        draft_cost, verify_cost = cost_tables
+        costs = draft_cost[num_reqs] + verify_cost[local_tokens]
+        accepted = np.concatenate(
+            ([num_reqs], num_reqs + np.cumsum(survival[valid][order]))
+        )
+        budget = int(np.argmax(accepted / costs))
+    return np.bincount(requests[:budget], minlength=num_reqs).astype(np.int32)
+
+
+class PCPAdaptiveVerification:
+    def __init__(self, pcp_size: int, shard_decode_requests: bool):
+        self.pcp_size = pcp_size
+        self.shard_decode_requests = shard_decode_requests
+        self.admitted_drafts: np.ndarray | None = None
+        self.num_tokens_per_req: np.ndarray | None = None
+
+    def plan(
+        self,
+        survival: np.ndarray,
+        scheduled_drafts: np.ndarray,
+        non_draft_tokens: np.ndarray,
+        cost_tables: tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray],
+        max_draft_budget: int,
+        has_prefill: bool,
+    ) -> int:
+        admitted = select_pcp_drafts(
+            survival,
+            scheduled_drafts,
+            non_draft_tokens,
+            cost_tables,
+            max_draft_budget,
+            self.pcp_size,
+            self.shard_decode_requests,
+            has_prefill,
+        )
+        # Both dimensions must agree on the complete layout, including ties.
+        admitted = get_tp_group().broadcast_object(admitted, src=0)
+        admitted = get_pcp_group().broadcast_object(admitted, src=0)
+        self.admitted_drafts = admitted
+        self.num_tokens_per_req = non_draft_tokens + admitted
+        return int(admitted.sum())
